entities.text: Eloori Venkatesham vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar
 Writ Petition No.31357 of 2023
Order:

Heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 3 and Sri Padma Rao Lakkaraju, learned Standing Counsel for National Highways Authority of India appearing for respondent No.4.
2.

The short grievance of the petitioners in this writ petition is that in spite of initiating proceedings under Section 3G (5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (for short, 'the Act, 1956') and issuing notices vide No.C2/192/2021, dated 21.09.2022 and 22.10.2022, respondent No.2 failed to consider and dispose of the application submitted by the petitioners by passing appropriate orders by considering their claim for enhancement of compensation in respect of the lands of the petitioners acquired under the Award proceedings No.C2/16/NH- 363/Kannala-II/2018, dated 24.01.2020.

It is the specific contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that this Court, on an earlier occasion in W.P.No.4886 of 2021, permitted the petitioners to make an application under Section 3G (5) of the Act, 1956 and further directed respondent No.2 herein to dispose of the said application within a period of four weeks by an order dated 28.07.2022.
In spite of the specific direction issued by this Court, respondent No.2 failed to comply with the said order and the application is still pending before him.
Hence, the petitioners once again approached this Court by filing the present writ petition.

3. Admittedly, this Court, on an earlier occasion in W.P.No.4886 of 2021, has already fixed the time for disposal of the application submitted by the petitioners under Section 3G (5) of the Act, 1956, it is obligatory on the part of respondent No.2 to dispose of the said application within the time prescribed by this Court.

But, unfortunately, the same is not complied with by respondent No.2.
4.
In the normal course, this Court should have initiated contempt proceedings against respondent No.2 for not complying with the order passed by this Court in W.P.No.4886 of 2021, dated 28.07.2022.

But, taking into consideration the fact that the Election Code is already operating in the State, this Court, for the time being, is refraining itself from initiating suo motu contempt proceedings against respondent No.2.
5.

In the light of the above, the writ petition is disposed of directing respondent No.2 to take steps for disposal of the application submitted by the petitioners vide proceedings No.C2/192/2021, dated 20.09.2022, as expeditiously as possible at any rate on or before 31.12.2023.
It is made clear that in case, if this order is not complied with by respondent No.2, the matter will be viewed seriously.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
